questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: You need to find a missing angle when two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, given one angle of 74°, using alternate angles. Which order of steps is correct?
options: Identify the transversal; spot the Z-shape formed; alternate angles are equal; answer = 74°
Identify the transversal; spot the Z-shape formed; alternate angles add to 180°; answer = 106°
Spot the F-shape formed; corresponding angles are equal; identify the transversal; answer = 74°
Assume the angle is co-interior; subtract from 180° first; then identify the transversal; answer = 106°
questions.answer: Identify the transversal; spot the Z-shape formed; alternate angles are equal; answer = 74°
questions.why: Alternate angles form a Z-shape and are always equal, so the correct sequence identifies the transversal, spots the Z, then applies equality to get 74°. Mixing up the shape or rule (like treating it as co-interior, which sums to 180°) gives the wrong angle.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A student classifies a shape: Step 1: It has four sides. Step 2: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. Step 3: All four angles are 90°. Step 4: Since all angles are equal, it must be a rhombus. Which step is WRONG?
options: Step 1: It has four sides
Step 2: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel
Step 3: All four angles are 90°
Step 4: Since all angles are equal, it must be a rhombus
questions.answer: Step 4: Since all angles are equal, it must be a rhombus
questions.why: A shape with four right angles and both pairs of sides parallel is a rectangle, not a rhombus — a rhombus is defined by equal side lengths, not equal angles. The student confused the property that defines a rhombus (equal sides) with the property that defines a rectangle (equal angles).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Solve for x: 4x = 20. Remember the rule — whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other. What is x?
questions.why: To undo ×4, divide both sides by 4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. x = 4 wrongly treats the equation as if 4 was subtracted; x = 16 comes from subtracting 4 instead of dividing; x = 24 comes from adding 4 to both sides instead of dividing.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Match each stage of human sexual reproduction to what happens at that stage: (1) Fertilisation, (2) Implantation, (3) Gestation. Which pairing is entirely correct?
options: Fertilisation = sperm and egg nuclei fuse; Implantation = embryo attaches to the uterus wall; Gestation = the baby develops over 9 months
Fertilisation = embryo attaches to the uterus wall; Implantation = sperm and egg nuclei fuse; Gestation = the baby develops over 9 months
Fertilisation = sperm and egg nuclei fuse; Implantation = the baby develops over 9 months; Gestation = embryo attaches to the uterus wall
Fertilisation = the baby develops over 9 months; Implantation = sperm and egg nuclei fuse; Gestation = embryo attaches to the uterus wall
questions.answer: Fertilisation = sperm and egg nuclei fuse; Implantation = embryo attaches to the uterus wall; Gestation = the baby develops over 9 months
questions.why: Fertilisation is the fusing of sperm and egg, implantation is when the resulting embryo attaches to the uterus wall, and gestation is the full developmental period afterwards. Swapping these stages mixes up the order in which they naturally occur.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Here are four statements about the Crusades. Which statement is FALSE?
options: The First Crusade set out in 1096 aiming to capture Jerusalem
Jerusalem was seen as holy by both Christians and Muslims
The Crusades were a single short campaign that ended after one battle
Crusader and Muslim forces fought over control of Jerusalem for almost 200 years
questions.answer: The Crusades were a single short campaign that ended after one battle
questions.why: The Crusades were actually a series of multiple campaigns (waves) stretching across almost two centuries, not one quick battle. Students sometimes picture it as a single event because only the First Crusade is usually studied in detail.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Three of these are examples of a CONSEQUENCE of an event, and one is a CAUSE. Which does NOT belong?
options: Peasants gained more bargaining power after the Black Death
Rising anger at the government followed poor harvests
Years of unfair taxation built up resentment among peasants
Labour shortages led to higher wages for workers
questions.answer: Years of unfair taxation built up resentment among peasants
questions.why: This statement describes a cause building up before an event, while the other three describe outcomes that happened AFTER an event. Students often mix up cause and consequence when both are written as flowing sentences.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Here are four statements about Magna Carta 1215. Which statement is FALSE?
options: Magna Carta established that even the king was subject to the law
Magna Carta is studied by historians as a primary source from 1215
Magna Carta gave every peasant in England the right to vote
Magna Carta was created partly to limit the monarch's power over nobles
questions.answer: Magna Carta gave every peasant in England the right to vote
questions.why: Magna Carta mainly protected the rights of nobles and limited royal power — it did not grant voting rights to peasants, which is a much later development. Students sometimes assume it created modern democratic rights immediately, but its impact was narrower and gradual.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student investigates whether the amount of salt added to water affects the boiling point of the water, keeping the volume of water the same in each test. Step 1: The amount of salt added is the independent variable, since the student changes it. Step 2: The boiling point of the water is the dependent variable, since it is measured. Step 3: The volume of water is the dependent variable, since it stays the same. Step 4: The controlled variable is anything kept the same, like the container used. Which step is WRONG?
options: Step 1: The amount of salt added is the independent variable, since the student changes it
Step 2: The boiling point of the water is the dependent variable, since it is measured
Step 3: The volume of water is the dependent variable, since it stays the same
Step 4: The controlled variable is anything kept the same, like the container used
questions.answer: Step 3: The volume of water is the dependent variable, since it stays the same
questions.why: Anything kept the same on purpose is a CONTROLLED variable, not a dependent one — the dependent variable is always what you measure as an outcome (here, boiling point). Confusing 'stays the same' with 'dependent' is the exact chronic mix-up: change = independent, measure = dependent, keep-same = controlled.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangular flag has a base of 12 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is its area?
options: 30 cm²
60 cm²
17 cm²
35 cm²
questions.why: Area of a triangle = (base × height) ÷ 2, so (12 × 5) ÷ 2 = 30 cm². A common error is forgetting to halve after multiplying, which gives 60 cm² instead.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and one angle is 118°. You need to find the co-interior (allied) angle on the other line. Which order of reasoning is correct?
options: Identify the transversal; spot the C-shape (or U-shape) formed; co-interior angles sum to 180°; answer = 62°
Identify the transversal; spot the Z-shape formed; co-interior angles are equal; answer = 118°
Spot the C-shape formed; co-interior angles are equal; identify the transversal; answer = 118°
Identify the transversal; assume corresponding angles; co-interior angles are equal; answer = 118°
questions.answer: Identify the transversal; spot the C-shape (or U-shape) formed; co-interior angles sum to 180°; answer = 62°
questions.why: Co-interior (allied) angles form a C-shape between the parallel lines and always add up to 180°, so 180° − 118° = 62°. Treating them as equal (like alternate or corresponding angles) is the common mix-up that leads students to wrongly answer 118°.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Three of these are examples of ASEXUAL reproduction, and one is NOT. Which does NOT belong?
options: A strawberry plant growing new plants from runners
Bacteria splitting into two identical cells
A human egg being fertilised by a sperm cell
A potato plant sprouting new plants from its tubers
questions.answer: A human egg being fertilised by a sperm cell
questions.why: Fertilisation of an egg by a sperm is sexual reproduction, since it combines genetic material from two parents, unlike the other examples which all produce genetically identical offspring from a single parent. The shared property of the other three is that they involve only one parent and no fusion of gametes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Your classmate says: 'In an experiment testing whether the type of music played to plants affects their growth height, the type of music is the dependent variable, because that's the interesting thing the scientist is studying.' Using an example of your own (not one already used with you before), explain what actually makes a variable independent, dependent, or controlled, and correct your classmate's mistake.
